assumptions: The initial product remains decision support with cited evidence and human final judgment rather than legal advice or an autonomous bid decision.
A CPV-defined Polish vertical can be selected without materially changing the subscription thesis.
Official TED and BZP access remains sufficiently lawful and operational for prototyping, subject to attribution, third-party rights, personal-data handling, and changing source terms.
The founder can use contractors or professional advisers for procurement-law, security, and data-contract work within the stated 30,000 PLN initial capital estimate.
The family renewable-energy company is treated only as a possible pilot lead, not as validated demand or permissioned data access.
No proprietary outcome-data advantage is credited until customers grant suitable rights and repeated collection demonstrates improved calibration.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Choose one CPV-defined vertical and obtain evidence from repeat bidders showing tender frequency, preparation hours and costs, detectable avoidable losses, and acceptable false-negative tolerance; then run paid pilots that record recommendation use, extraction accuracy and reviewer time, hours or losses saved, trial-to-paid conversion, CAC, support and model costs, retention, payback, and explicit contractual rights to reuse anonymized decision and outcome labels. A credible higher score would also require head-to-head proof of a material workflow or economic advantage over the named alternatives.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A new tender creates a recurring, observable resource-allocation decision, and avoiding work on an ineligible or poor-fit bid can create measurable value. The insight is credible, but AI-assisted matching and go/no-go scoring are already marketed by multiple Polish products, so the distinctive insight is the proposed client-specific decision loop rather than the basic gate itself.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Offer-preparation cost is real, the notice stream is large, and SMEs submit most offers below EU thresholds. However, the packet does not quantify avoidable loss in a chosen vertical or establish that a decision owner will trust the recommendation and pay 499-1,499 PLN monthly; free official alerts and overlapping products priced from 69 to 599 PLN materially constrain the current pricing hypothesis.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Advance-paid subscription software could have attractive cash conversion, operating leverage, and gross margin once a vertical template stabilizes. Yet pricing, CAC, conversion, churn, retention, inference and OCR cost, document QA, onboarding, support, liability burden, contribution margin, payback, and owner earnings are all unvalidated, while public competitor pricing is mostly below the proposed range.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Poland has a substantial recurring procurement market, with roughly 153,000 contracts awarded in 2024 and meaningful SME participation. The proposed beachhead is still only 'a narrow technical category': no CPV niche is bound to evidence for qualified-notice frequency, repeat-bidder count, preparation cost, or addressable revenue, so its combination of narrowness and economic sufficiency is unresolved.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: The founder can own the scoring software and direct customer relationship, but official search and alerts are free and at least three Polish vendors already advertise AI matching, SWZ analysis, risk assessment, or explicit bid verdicts. No exclusive channel, embedded workflow, proprietary dataset, or demonstrated vertical superiority currently supports a dominant position.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: If one vertical produces a trusted decision workflow and reusable rule set, adjacent CPV categories, customer segments, EU notices, deadline management, requirement review, and outcome analytics are logical extensions. Expansion remains conditional on first proving a beachhead and collecting legally reusable customer outcome labels.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Independently written code is ownable, but the underlying notices are nonexclusive, openly reusable, and already used by commercial platforms. A consented dataset of internal bid decisions, effort, margin, and outcomes could compound, but no rights, collection workflow, account base, or calibration advantage is yet established; presently the mechanism is replaceable.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Cited requirement extraction plus a customer-specific decision log could become more useful than generic alerts, but the packet shows no measured gain in accuracy, time saved, disqualifications avoided, win economics, trust, or UX versus incumbent products. The proposed price premium therefore lacks a demonstrated performance or workflow advantage.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Anonymous official API access, commercially reusable notice data, large digital notice volume, and current AI capabilities make a low-capital prototype timely. The same conditions lower entry barriers, and the presence of several current AI competitors suggests the window is active but not early or uncontested.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Narrow-sector outbound, self-serve trials, consultants, trade groups, and the founder's family-company connection offer plausible first-customer routes without personal-brand dependence. Competitors demonstrate low-friction signup, but there is no evidence for this product's reachable repeat-bidder list, lead cost, conversion, sales cycle, referral terms, or four-month CAC payback.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The software and analytical work fit the founder's data-science skills, AI leverage, capital limit, and part-time constraints, and initial source access does not require a bilateral deal. Execution risk is material because official data can be incomplete or wrong, documents vary and may be practically restricted, false negatives can forfeit valuable opportunities, and legal-review, QA, security, support, and liability demands may exceed a five-hour daily budget.

highest_value_structural_change: Make the product a deeply vertical, customer-economics decision system rather than another tender monitor: integrate client eligibility rules, capacity, margin, preparation effort, and post-decision outcomes into an auditable gate, contract for reusable anonymized labels from inception, and price against verified savings in one CPV niche. This creates a differentiated workflow and a plausible compounding asset that public-feed competitors do not automatically possess.
main_structural_strength: A high-frequency, externally observable trigger can anchor an advance-paid software subscription, while open official feeds permit a low-capital prototype and the founder can own both the scoring layer and direct SME relationship.
primary_score_limiter: The current product has neither a demonstrated vertical-specific advantage nor control of the proposed permissioned outcome-data asset, leaving willingness to pay, retention, acquisition efficiency, and durable differentiation unresolved against cheaper direct substitutes.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: At least three current Polish products already advertise substantially overlapping AI matching, SWZ analysis, risk scoring, or explicit STARTUJ/ROZWAZ/POMIN verdicts, commonly at public prices below v1's proposed 499-1,499 PLN monthly range, while the official platform supplies free search and daily alerts.
